themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked to 3 reports this week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week, a 1,100% increase (z-score: 6.35), suggesting either rapid deterioration of signage infrastructure or a coordinated removal pattern affecting navigation and traffic safety in Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 3 street sign complaints filed this week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35)
1,100% spike represents statistical anomaly indicating acute rather than chronic issue
Timing suggests possible weather event, infrastructure failure, or vandalism pattern
reporting_angles: Walk the district to document which signs are missing and map the pattern geographically
Interview DOT about maintenance schedules and whether this aligns with known issues
Check if vandalism or theft pattern is coordinated or if this reflects deferred maintenance

themes_detail.label: Lot Conditions Deteriorating Rapidly
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints reached 4 this week, a 1,500% spike from the 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.67), indicating acute blight concerns possibly tied to abandonment, debris accumulation, or property code enforcement gaps in Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 4 lot condition complaints filed this week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,500% increase, z-score: 5.67)
Convergence with broader 'Dirty Condition' spike (114 complaints last week vs. 31.9 avg, up 258%)
Aligns with repeated CB budget requests for park improvements and neighborhood aesthetics
reporting_angles: Identify which lots are generating complaints and document conditions; interview owners/city about remediation timelines
Connect to broader sanitation surge: are lots, streets, and buildings all experiencing coordinated neglect or is this post-weather cleanup lag?
Explore whether code enforcement is responding or if properties are in limbo during ULURP/rezoning processes

themes_detail.label: Cleanliness Crisis Spreading
themes_detail.summary: Dirty condition complaints surged to 114 last week versus 31.9 weekly average, a 258% increase (z-score: 6.61), marking the third-highest spike in the dataset and signaling district-wide sanitation breakdown across streets, lots, and possibly building exteriors.
evidence: 114 dirty condition complaints last week vs. 31.9 weekly average (258% spike, z-score: 6.61)
Concurrent spike in litter basket requests (7 last week vs. 0.8 avg, +833%) suggests overwhelmed waste infrastructure
Dirty condition ranks 7th overall volume (518 over 90 days) and is now accelerating—indicates recent deterioration not long-running baseline
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about collection frequency, staffing levels, and whether sanitation routes have been reduced or delayed in Bed-Stuy
Canvass affected blocks to identify hotspots; speak to residents and business owners about when conditions worsened
Cross-check against trash/litter enforcement ticketing data: is DSNY issuing violations for illegal dumping or are complaints going unaddressed?

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints jumped to 8 last week from a 3.1 weekly baseline, a 156% increase (z-score: 6.24), suggesting emerging health code violations or inadequate inspection coverage at restaurants and food vendors in Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 8 food establishment complaints last week vs. 3.1 weekly average (156% increase, z-score: 6.24)
Community Board has standing budget request to increase health and safety inspections for restaurants and childcare programs
311 data does not specify violation type (rodents, temperature, sanitation), requiring DOHMH follow-up for detail
reporting_angles: Obtain DOHMH inspection records and violation grades for restaurants cited in 311 complaints; identify patterns (chain vs. independent, cuisine type, geography)
Interview DOHMH about inspection staffing and whether Bed-Stuy is under-resourced relative to complaint volume
Speak to restaurant owners and community advocates about whether this reflects new violations or long-standing enforcement gaps surfacing now

themes_detail.label: Tree and Vegetation Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints hit 3 two weeks ago (2,300% spike, z-score: 8.69) and overgrown tree/branch complaints reached 8 three weeks ago (611% spike, z-score: 5.9), indicating severe tree health or maintenance breakdown affecting block-by-block safety and aesthetics.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2,300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
8 overgrown tree/branch complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average (611% spike, z-score: 5.9)
Converges with repeated CB budget requests for 'new or expanded park or amenity' suggesting chronic underinvestment in green space maintenance
reporting_angles: Work with NYC Parks to obtain inventory of flagged trees and pruning schedules in Bed-Stuy; identify which blocks are most affected
Document hazardous overhanging branches and dead trees on street—photo story potential
Interview residents and community board about whether tree complaints are new or long-standing; connect to development pressure and gentrification patterns
